subject: gk
question: ________ refers to relaxation of government restrictions.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liberalisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Liberalisation** refers to the relaxation or removal of government restrictions and regulations in areas like trade, investment, and industries.
 
• It typically aims to encourage private sector participation, enhance competition, and improve economic efficiency.
 
• The process of liberalisation gained momentum in India with the **1991 Economic Reforms**, which marked a significant shift towards a market-driven economy.
 
• Key reforms under liberalisation include reductions in import tariffs, deregulation of industries, and easing restrictions on foreign investments.
 
• The goal of liberalisation is to foster economic growth, attract foreign investments, and integrate the domestic economy with the global market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privatisation:**

 
 
• Privatisation refers to the transfer of ownership, management, or control of government-owned enterprises to the private sector.
 
• It is aimed at improving efficiency, profitability, and performance of these enterprises.
 
• Examples in India include disinvestment in Air India and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL).
 
 
 
• **Globalisation:**
 
 
• Globalisation refers to the integration of economies, societies, and cultures through trade, investment, technology, and information flows.
 
• It has led to increased interdependence among nations and a more interconnected global economy.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment:**
 
 
• Disinvestment involves selling or liquidating government-owned assets or shares in public sector enterprises.
 
• The goal is to reduce the fiscal burden, improve efficiency, and promote public-private partnerships.
 
 
 
• **India’s 1991 Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991, prompting economic reforms under the leadership of then-Finance Minister Manmohan Singh.
 
• The reforms were based on the principles of liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation (LPG model).
 
• They included measures like devaluation of the Indian rupee, tax reforms, and opening up of various sectors to foreign investments.
